page: Microsoft Azure D8als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dalv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read bandwidth is relatively weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Large-block write bandwidth remains average.

The server's hardware profile makes it suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints, such as text processing, web serving, and lightweight software compilation. It also demonstrates strong performance in small-model LLM text generation. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio represents a tradeoff, making this instance less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data analytics. The lack of bundled local storage requires external storage provisioning for persistent data.
